model: CTC heat pumps and controllers via BMS (Modbus TCP)
applies_to: CTC EcoHeat 400, EcoZenith i250/i350/i550, EcoVent i350F, GSi/GS, EcoPart 6xx M/Pro and EcoLogic controllers whose display has three ports (Ethernet), BMS document 16260016-3 (CR01143, 2026-02-02).
summary: CTC's heat pumps and system controllers expose a BMS register list over Modbus TCP from the display's Ethernet port. Everything is a 16-bit holding register: a 1000-block of control values the BMS must refresh, settings from 61500 (hot water, heating circuits 1-4, curves, cooling, pool, solar, add-on heat), and read-only values from 62000 (temperatures, heat pump status, pressures, compressor speed, energy and smart-grid state). Each setting has companion registers holding its max, min and step.

addressing.note: The document says the base address is always 0 ('Offset: 0'), so the printed register number is the wire address: 61502 is requested as 61502 and 1000 as 1000. All registers are above standard Modbus numbering (larger than 49999) except the 1000/1100 control block.

source.title: Building Management System (BMS)
source.pages: Swedish pp. 1-11, English from p. 12: p. 13 general data, pp. 14-15 how to read the list, pp. 16-17 control registers and virtual inputs, pp. 19-21 alarms, pp. 23-44 complete BMS list

notes: Data type follows the 'Signed' column: 1 = INT16, 0 = UINT16. Scale is the 'Factor' column. Units are not printed in the list; °C is given here only where the row text names a temperature or °C, and other units only where the row text names them.

The 1000-block (p. 23) has no factor or signed column. Only rows with printed codes are included (1005, 1007, 1015-1019, 1022, 1100). The setpoint, RPS and immersion-heater limit rows (1000-1004, 1006, 1008-1014, 1020, 1021, 1023-1033) are left out because their scaling is not stated; 1003/1004 are also printed with upper and lower tank swapped between the table and the text on p. 16.

Cascades of up to 10 heat pumps (A1-A10) repeat each heat pump value in consecutive registers. Only heat pump A1 is listed: for A2-A10 add 1-9 to the A1 register (e.g. A1 status 62017, A2 62018 ... A10 62026; blocked flags 61521-61530; max RPS 61572-61581). The same holds for the compressor 32-bit counters, which step by 2 (62214, 62216 ... 62232 and 62341, 62343 ... 62359).

32-bit counters are printed as two rows, the LSB word first and the MSB word ('<< 16') in the next register, so they are listed as UINT32 with low word first (CDAB). The immersion heater kWh counter is split differently: low word 62191, high word 62329.

Each 615xx-617xx setting has read-only companion registers in the 600xx range holding its max, min and step (quoted in the description), and a visibility bit (column 'Visible' register and 'Bit') showing whether the parameter is active for the installed product.
Which product supports each row is marked per model in the source table; check it before relying on a register. Rows with no function text (61627, 61628, 62285-62287) are left out.

Alarm and information texts: read 65133 first (high byte = number of info texts, low byte = number of alarms), then 65010-65059 (alarm pairs: HP flag, alarm code) and 65060-65069 (info pairs). These buffer registers are described but not listed here.

integration.summary: Define 'Modbus TCP' under Installer/Define/Remote control on a three-port display, then read 62000-62365 with function 3 and write the 1000-block (refreshed at least every 5 minutes) with function 16. Use the 615xx settings sparingly.
integration.enable: In the display menu Installer > Define > Remote control, define 'Modbus TCP' (connection through the display's Ethernet port). Only displays with three connection ports support BMS over TCP/IP.
integration.watchdog: The 1000-block control registers must be rewritten within 5 minutes or they are reset; they are also reset on restart.
quirks: Base address must be set to 0 in the master; registers are above 49999.
Read with function 3, write with function 16; at most 100 registers per transfer.
Read 65133 before reading alarm/info buffers, because the read fills them.
setup: Connect the BMS to the display's Ethernet port; the document recommends testing with QModMaster.
gotchas: The 615xx-617xx settings are stored with a limited number of write cycles; frequent writes can damage the controller. Use the 1000-block for values that change often.
SmartGrid priority is remote control (BMS/contact) first, then myUplink, week schedule, then the setting.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
note: Re-typed from the manufacturer's public documentation (see source) and verified against it. Registers vary by firmware and options; verify against the live device before writing.
